text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Number of jobseekers decreases by 12,000 in October to 3.1 million, according to French Labour Ministry. But by ILO standards, figure rises by 14,000 people.
-- Paris prosecutor opens a criminal investigation into suspected fraud and issuing of misleading information at state bank Credit Lyonnais in the early 1990s.
-- CNAM French health insurance fund said it spent 37.99 billion francs in October, down 0.1 percent from September and 0.2 percent lower than October 1995 spending.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says his position over planned GEC-Alsthom and Framatome merger is not irreconcilable with government's wish to maintain French control over the nuclear reactor manufacturer.
-- Bank specialising in small and medium-sized firms, BDPME, to receive a 740-million-franc recapitalisation from state-owned Caisse des Depots and the state.
-- Market operators expect Bundesbank and Bank of France to ease interest rates.
-- New car registrations in France fell 21.7 percent in November.
-- Media group Hachette Livre buys 25 percent of publisher Ramsay-Lafon.
L'AGEFI

-- European finance ministers reach partial agreement on future monetary stability pact, define sanctions to be applied to countries running excessive deficits but do not agree on specific criteria defining excessive deficits.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Finance ministry says early retirement and lower labour charges negotiated with truck drivers and employers may cost state up to one billion francs.
-- Air Liquide wins big contract in Italy.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- French fishermen defy British ban on fishing in Channel waters south of Guernsey and Sark Islands.
-- EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert asks France to freeze production volumes and market shares of new entity to be formed by Thomson Multimedia and Daewoo as conditions for approval for privatisation.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE

-- Bundesbank head Hans Tietmeyer says does not accept view that France and Germany's other neighbours bore a heavy burden from German re-unification, adds has never been outvoted in Bundesbank decisions.
